observations: Photo 0: bare engine assembly (no transmission/gearbox attached) sitting on bare ground in what looks like a used-parts yard.
Photo 0: plastic intake manifold with multiple hose/sensor wiring visible, watermark 'ALEX AUTO ALEXANDER' overlaid, no engine code or casting number visible on the block.
Photo 1: same engine from a different angle, showing a flywheel/flexplate with visible orange-brown surface rust/oxidation and many mounting holes.
No VIN plate, casting stamp, or engine code sticker is legible in either photo.
No video, sound, or compression-test evidence of the engine running.

claims.claim: Implied fit for 2008/2010/2012 Camry model years
claims.evidence: No chassis/VIN match or fitment documentation shown in photos.

risks.risk: Unknown mechanical condition - no proof engine runs or starts

risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for-parts condition

risks.risk: Visible rust/oxidation on flywheel and hardware suggests prolonged outdoor storage or water exposure
risks.proof: Close-up photos of cylinder bores, oil pan interior, or a borescope clip showing internal condition
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming internal corrosion risk, discounted accordingly

risks.risk: Unknown mileage/usage history (no odometer or prior vehicle documentation)

Video of the engine cranking or running with sound
Compression test results or borescope video of cylinder bores
Photo of donor vehicle's odometer or any paperwork tying this engine to a specific Camry
Full set of photos from all sides showing what accessories/sensors are included
response.reason: The seller's core claim ('2GR') that determines whether this is a V6 or 4-cylinder Camry engine cannot be confirmed from either photo since no engine code or ID plate is visible, and this distinction drives a large price gap; a worst-case price cannot be set without first resolving engine identity.
